title: Floor by floor
statement:
A building's emergency plan is a binary tree: each node is a room, and its children are the rooms reached next. The fire marshal wants the rooms listed floor by floor, left to right.

Return a list of floors, where each floor is the list of room numbers at that depth, from the top floor down. In tests, a tree is written as a level-order array with nulls.

clarifyingQuestions.question: What should an empty tree return?
Within a floor, what order?
clarifyingQuestions.why: Determines the order children are enqueued.

clarifyingQuestions.question: How big can the tree be?

approaches.name: BFS with a queue, level by level
approaches.idea: Process all nodes of the current level, collecting their children as the next level.

approaches.name: DFS with depth
approaches.idea: Recursively visit nodes, appending each value to the list for its depth, visiting left before right.
approaches.tradeoffs: Also correct; order within a floor relies on visiting left first.

optimal.name: Level-by-level BFS
optimal.explanation: Keep the current level as a list. Record its values, then build the next level from each node’s left and right children in order. Stop when a level is empty.

hintLadder: Which traversal visits nodes in order of depth?
How can you tell where one floor ends and the next begins?
What if you process one whole level at a time?
Use BFS and take the whole current level before moving to its children.

expectedMentions.what: Proposes breadth-first search with O(n) time
States the space as the widest level
Traces the example level by level

followUps: Return the floors in zigzag order, alternating direction.
Return only the rightmost room on each floor.

walkthrough.say: Empty tree returns an empty list, and within each floor I go left to right?

Floor by floor is breadth-first search. The only extra thing is knowing where each floor ends. If I process an entire level at once and build the next level from its children, each list is one floor. O(n) time, and space for the widest level.
Start with the root as the first level.
Children in left-to-right order become the next level.
For 7 with children 3 and 9, where 9 has 8 and 12: first level 7, then 3 and 9. 3 has no children and 9 gives 8 and 12. Then the next level is empty. Result 7, then 3, 9, then 8, 12.
For a left chain 1, 2, 3, each level has one node, so three floors of one.
O(n) time and O(w) space where w is the widest floor.
